items.t: Ernie Johnson Is Leaving Inside The NBA,' And Now We're All Getting Emotional
items.x: Mitchell Layton There are a few things you can always count on in this world: someone bringing potato salad to the cookout, someone asking, “if they can be honest,” about being rude as hell, and Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer Ernie Johnson on your television. For over 50 years, Johnson has worked in television, starting as a news anchor in 1979 and, for the past 36 years, hosting "Inside the NBA" with a revolving cast of guests that settled on Kenny Smith, Charles Barkley and Shaquille O’Neal. On Wednesday, Johnson announced in a social media post that he will retire from hosting the show that has become as much a part of the NBA as basketball itself. "It's just time," Johnson, 70, said, adding that he would keep working, including covering the NCAA men's basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. items.t: The Dream Continues: Atlanta Forces Historic Game 7 In The WNBA Finals
items.x: Jonathan Bachman / Atlanta Dream / Angel Reese ATL HOE. That's the feeling in Atlanta after the Dream ties up the WNBA Finals 80-69 to force a deciding Game 7 against the Golden State Valkyries. The Dream came out hot, scoring 30 points in the first quarter after failing to reach that mark in the first half of Game 5. Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray scored 21 points each, while Angel Reese added 15 points, 14 rebounds, and 6 assists, returning to double-double form. Her two three-pointers extend the Dream's win streak when she scores at least one. Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 26 points, but it was too little, too late. items.t: Beloved Italian restaurant Mezzaluna is scheduled to close
items.x: UPPER EAST SIDE (PIX11) — After more than 40 years of serving the Upper East Side, beloved Italian restaurant Mezzaluna is preparing to say goodbye. ( WNCN ) A North Carolina town that sustained gas line breaks, a water pipe rupture, and other problems associated with a Google Fiber vendor has halted all work and forced the company to clean up ahead of Halloween. items.x: ROCKY MOUNT, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A second tax preparer in Rocky Mount has pleaded guilty to participating in a six-year scheme that led to the theft of nearly $4 million in tax money , the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of North Carolina said Wednesday. According to federal prosecutors, Chowan Watson and Angela Dickens were the operators of the Rocky Mount-based Empire Tax Service, which was renamed K&J Tax Service. From 2017 to 2023, according to federal prosecutors, Watson and Dickens fraudulently filed hundreds of tax returns by inflating the "Other 1099 Withholding" amounts, allowing them to take excessive fees from the inflated taxpayer refunds. Prosecutors said the scheme resulted in a tax loss of about $3.9 million. The culture celebrated diamond chains, fleets of exotic sports cars, sprawling mansions, and designer wardrobes. And these symbols of arrival were deeply important. The Trenton woman, 46, allegedly went to his Clinton Township property Tuesday, October 27. His security called police, WDIV reported . Savage was arraigned Wednesday in 41B District Court on aggravated stalking, carrying up to five years. Bond was $250,000 cash or surety, without a 10 percent option. Release requires GPS monitoring; she cannot contact Eminem, have weapons or leave Michigan. Authorities did not explain the earlier order. A separate case involving Matthew David Hughes brought a prison sentence on June 17, 2025. As AllHipHop previously reported , a jury convicted Hughes of aggravated stalking and first-degree home invasion after he entered the rapper's property in August 2024. His sentence requires at least 18 years in prison before he can seek parole.

items.t: Gathering of 100 Black Men in Waynesboro encourages community involvement and voter participation
items.x: WAYNESBORO, Ga. (WJBF) – With Election Day just days away, men of all ages gathered in Waynesboro Thursday evening for an event focused on community unity, leadership and the importance of voting. The event, called “The Gathering of 100 Black Men,” took place at City Park on October 29 under the theme “When Black Men Vote We Win.” Local leaders, pastors, elected officials and community members came together to encourage civic engagement and show younger generations why their voices matter. Augusta Judicial Circuit District Attorney Jared Williams said seeing men of different ages come together made the event especially meaningful. “We had young men all the way from four years old up to, well, I won’t say how old some of these jokers are, but it’s been a great opportunity just to be with the people and to talk about something as important as voting,” Williams said. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Sen. Darline Graham votes in Lexington, talks campaign’s final days
items.x: LEXINGTON, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Sen. Darline Graham cast her ballot in Lexington on Thursday afternoon alongside her family. The vote follows President Donald Trump's visit to Rock Hill earlier in the day. Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina Graham said she spoke with the president about Russia sanctions and could speak with him again before Election Day. She said she has campaigned across South Carolina to earn voters' support. “I have worked from one end of this state to the other. I start early in the morning and I don’t end until late at night,” Graham said. Asked about not receiving support from Congressman Ralph Norman, Graham said a write-in vote is essentially a vote for Democratic candidate Dr. Annie Andrews. Early voting ends Oct. 31, with Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

items.t: Breast cancer patients receive special care kits from Augusta Coca-Cola
items.x: AUGUSTA, Ga. (WJBF) – Some patients at the Georgia Cancer Center received a special gift on Thursday. Breast cancer patient care kits were put together by employees at the Augusta Coca Cola plant and distributed to patients on Oct. 29. Kits included wool hats, socks, and water bottles. "The patients always love to get goodies to know that others are thinking of them and the personal note, we also give another gift, pillows to our breast cancer patients," Andrea Rhoden, a breast nurse navigator. "To kind of brighten somebody's day, in the midst of chaos of their life," said Corey Holloway of Augusta Coca Cola, "hopefully this is something that will put a smile on their face, to just to feel warm inside and to make them feel better." The kits were given to patients at 14 breast cancer clinics in the Southeast. October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Photojournalist credit: Regynal McKie

items.t: New South Carolina law expands homicide-by-child-abuse charges to all minors
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. ( WSPA ) – A new South Carolina law closes a legal loophole involving child abuse deaths. PREVIOUS STORY | South Carolina law protects abuse victims under 18 Before the change, homicide-by-child-abuse charges could only be filed when the victim was 11 or younger. Gov. Henry McMaster signed the bill into law last Thursday, expanding homicide-by-child-abuse protections to all victims under 18. If a child older than 11 died as a result of abuse or neglect, prosecutors were required to pursue murder or other criminal charges instead of a homicide-by-child-abuse charge. State Senate President Thomas Alexander introduced the bill in March 2025. He said lawmakers may not have realized the age restriction prevented prosecutors from pursuing stronger charges in some cases. “There were cases that were not able to be made, charges that were not able to be made,” he said. items.x: WILKES COUNTY, Ga. (WJBF) – A second arrest has been made in the death of a child in Atlanta, according to the Wilkes County Sheriff's Office on Thursday. items.t: Patrick Stewart, stage giant also of ‘Star Trek’ and ‘X-Men’ fame, dies at 86
items.x: (AP) Patrick Stewart , the classically trained stage actor who scaled the Shakespearean canon and added gravitas to a “Star Trek” franchise and the “X-Men” films, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the "X-Men" and "Star Trek: The Next Generation" series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of "A Christmas Carol" and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter's "No Man's Land" and Samuel Beckett's "Waiting for Godot" in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen.

Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year

items.t: Memphis-Shelby County Schools graduation rate hits 7-year high
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. Memphis-Shelby County Schools is celebrating the district's highest graduation rate in seven years. On Thursday, MSCS said the graduation rate rose to 85.4% for the 2025–26 school year. The rate increased 1% from 84.4% in 2024–25 and 7.7% from 77.7% in 2020, MSCS said. The seven- year series compares annual results for different graduating classes. Shelby County Commission vote on MSCS battle MSCS said the comparison looks at annual district results for different graduating classes and does not follow the same students over seven years. "Every student who crosses the graduation stage represents years of effort by that student, their family, and the educators and staff who supported them. We celebrate this progress and remain focused on strengthening the support every student needs to finish with a strong path forward," said Dr. Roderick F. Richmond, superintendent of MSCS.

Morley, 28, escaped Sunday night from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville while serving a life sentence for the 2022 murder of Cody Birchfield. items.t: Overlooked, overstimulated, and finally seen: Black women on late ADHD Diagnoses
items.x: A growing number of Black women are getting ADHD diagnoses as adults and advocates like Brianne Saturdays are helping them make sense of it. Brianne Saturdays remembers standing in the middle of her kitchen, screaming at the top of her lungs while her kids screamed and the TV blared, and asking herself: “What is wrong with me? Why am I so overstimulated? Why can’t I focus?’” It would take years, and five psychiatrists, before she got an answer: ADHD. She’s one of a growing number of Black women, including actress Tisha Campbell, who was diagnosed at 57, sharing their experiences with late-in-life ADHD diagnoses. According to the CDC, about 15.5 million U.S. adults have ADHD, and more than half were diagnosed as adults. His father says school officials recently informed him that two students had been suspended for bullying his son. A Ghanaian teenager who moved to New York City in hopes of building a better future was fatally shot Thursday morning while reportedly walking to school in the Bronx. Now, his grieving father believes bullying may have played a role in his son’s death. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Woman, juvenile hospitalized in critical condition after incident in Hawthorne
items.x: Two people, including a juvenile, were hospitalized in critical condition after an incident in Hawthorne Thursday. Hawthorne Police were called to a residence on the 4000 block of 139th Street around 3:20 p.m. Paramedics transported a woman and a juvenile to the hospital. Emergency room doctors said the woman was pronounced death imminent, while the juvenile remained in critical condition. Details are limited and the circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear. Footage from the scene showed Hawthorne police and Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department detectives surrounding an apartment complex and they collected evidence. Neither the woman nor the juvenile’s identities were released. Anyone with information about the incident is urged to call LASD’s Homicide Bureau at 323-890-5500. items.t: L.A. DASH buses to begin ticketing illegally parked drivers with cameras
items.x: Drivers who illegally park in bus lanes or at bus stops in Los Angeles could soon receive tickets in the mail as the city rolls out a new camera enforcement program. Beginning Monday, Nov. 2, the Los Angeles Department of Transportation will use cameras installed on DASH buses to identify vehicles illegally parked in bus lanes and bus stops, city officials announced Thursday. For the first 60 days, drivers will receive warning notices rather than fines. Paid citations will begin Jan. 2, 2027. The system uses two forward-facing cameras mounted behind the windshields of DASH buses to automatically detect and record potential parking violations. LADOT personnel will review the footage before citations are issued. Warning notices and citations will be mailed to the registered owners of vehicles found in violation. items.t: La Brea Tar Pits museum is getting its first major renovation in nearly 50 years
items.x: A new chapter is beginning at the La Brea Tar Pits, and a groundbreaking ceremony was held Thursday to kick off the next phase of the historic site. The La Brea Tar Pits are known for preserving the past 50,000 years of history, to be exact. But now the focus is on the future, with construction already underway on the new Page Museum, which will change how visitors experience the Ice Age. The Natural History Museums of Los Angeles County, which oversees La Brea Tar Pits, launched the multi-year plan to reimagine the 13-acre site, the first renovation since the museum opened to the public in 1977. New renderings show plans for a new entrance along Wilshire Boulevard, a larger theater and walking paths connecting the museum to its famous fossil exhibits. items.t: Sir Patrick Stewart of ‘Star Trek’ and ‘X-Men’ has died at 86
items.x: Famed British actor Sir Patrick Stewart, known for his iconic roles in "Star Trek: The Next Generation" and "X-Men," has passed away. He was 86 years old. He passed away on Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles "in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," a statement posted on his official X account read. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," the statement continued. "We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace." items.x: Twenty-nine years after a pregnant 15-year-old girl was found slain on an Oxnard embankment, there is a renewed plea for information to help identify her killer. On Oct. 29, 1997, a bicyclist riding on Victoria Avenue, south of the Santa Clara River bridge, found Gabriela "Gabi" Maldonado dead from gunshot wounds to her head and abdomen. Investigators later determined that Maldonado was eight months pregnant , according to the Ventura County Sheriff's Office. Maldonado's 21-year-old boyfriend at the time, and possible father of her unborn baby, Edgar Alberto Fuentes, was arrested on suspicion of murder shortly after her body was found. items.t: El Niño-linked waves push California water levels to historic highs
items.x: Ocean water levels along the California coast are reaching some of their highest readings in more than a century, with massive underwater waves linked to El Niño contributing to the unusually high seas, federal officials say. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) reported Wednesday that tide stations across California have recorded new or broken water level records, including readings in Los Angeles, San Diego, La Jolla and Santa Barbara. The elevated levels are being driven by a combination of unusually high tides associated with the full moon and the moon's close approach to Earth, along with oceanic Kelvin waves moving north along the West Coast, according to NOAA. NOAA data shows unusually high water levels exceeding the minor flooding threshold in La Jolla, California, in October 2026. items.x: Moussa Diawara, a 57-year-old from Mali , lived in the United States for nearly half his life, where he married and had two children who are U.S. citizens. He worked and paid taxes but was deported to Ghana by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement during the summer. According to CBS News , Diawara first entered the U.S. on a tourist visa at the age of 32 but overstayed it and later sought refugee protection, fearing persecution if he were to return to Mali, a predominantly Muslim country, as he had converted to Christianity. items.t: Sen. Darline Graham votes in Lexington, talks campaign’s final days
items.x: LEXINGTON, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Sen. Darline Graham cast her ballot in Lexington on Thursday afternoon alongside her family. The vote follows President Donald Trump's visit to Rock Hill earlier in the day. Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina Graham said she spoke with the president about Russia sanctions and could speak with him again before Election Day. She said she has campaigned across South Carolina to earn voters' support. “I have worked from one end of this state to the other. I start early in the morning and I don’t end until late at night,” Graham said. Asked about not receiving support from Congressman Ralph Norman, Graham said a write-in vote is essentially a vote for Democratic candidate Dr. Annie Andrews. Early voting ends Oct. 31, with Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

items.t: Benedictine dominates Groves on senior night
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — Benedictine football defeated Groves 49-6 on its senior night at Memorial Stadium Thursday night. items.t: Liberty County basketball ready for new classification
items.x: HINESVILLE, Ga. (WSAV) — Liberty County basketball will begin its first season in Region 3-AAAA after it moved up from Region 3-AAA in the offseason. The Panthers are coming off a solid 15-9 season where they finished second in Region 3-AAA with a record of 12-2 in region play. The success was also a big jump from the year before when they finished 11-11. Head coach Levon Grant said his team is prepared to take on the classification change. "We tend to worry about the things going on right here in this gym," said Grant. "We have a lot of juniors and seniors that made a big impact last year, and when you have that, you tend to focus on yourself." Liberty County will begin the season hosting Wayne County on Nov. 19.

items.x: HINESVILLE, Ga. (WSAV) — Fort Stewart officials unveiled a new driving training course for tactical vehicles Thursday. The course lets soldiers get behind the wheel and learn how to maneuver through the kind of challenging terrain they could face in combat. The 37-acre course started as nothing more than a field of pine trees. In less than 100 days, soldiers at Fort Stewart transformed it into a training course built from the ground up. It's designed to prepare soldiers for the unexpected while giving them a safe place to train for dangerous real-world situations. From uneven terrain to crossing wet gaps in the land, the driving range puts soldiers and their tactical vehicles to the test. "So this is really building soldiers' lethality and readiness, making them more confident in their abilities to move," said Lieutenant Colonel William Watts. items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. ( WSPA ) – A new South Carolina law closes a legal loophole involving child abuse deaths. PREVIOUS STORY | South Carolina law protects abuse victims under 18 Before the change, homicide-by-child-abuse charges could only be filed when the victim was 11 or younger. Gov. Henry McMaster signed the bill into law last Thursday, expanding homicide-by-child-abuse protections to all victims under 18. If a child older than 11 died as a result of abuse or neglect, prosecutors were required to pursue murder or other criminal charges instead of a homicide-by-child-abuse charge. State Senate President Thomas Alexander introduced the bill in March 2025. He said lawmakers may not have realized the age restriction prevented prosecutors from pursuing stronger charges in some cases. “There were cases that were not able to be made, charges that were not able to be made,” he said. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: New SC law requires restaurants to disclose imported shrimp starting Wednesday
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) A new South Carolina law aimed at increasing transparency for seafood consumers takes effect Wednesday, requiring restaurants and other food service establishments to disclose when they serve imported shrimp. The law , signed by Gov. Henry McMaster on June 30, requires establishments that serve imported shrimp to post notices on menus and at their main entrances informing customers that they may serve imported shrimp. The measure took effect 120 days after the governor signed it. Under the law, businesses that serve both domestic and imported shrimp must display a notice stating: "Some items served at this establishment may contain foreign imported shrimp. Ask for more information." Establishments that serve only imported shrimp must post a notice stating that some menu items contain foreign imported shrimp. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year

items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.x: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) – The Dayton Police Department is introducing the Runaway, Outreach, Notification, and Intervention (RONI) pilot program to connect at-risk youth and their families with support services. The program is made possible through a partnership with Daybreak. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight we’ll lose in Nashville News 2's sister station, WAVY, went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.x: (NewsNation) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy, better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5% last month and was up 3.6% relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5% month-over-month and 3.6% relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7in July to 3.4% in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2% from August to September, after increasing by 4.4% from July to August. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: West Virginia #9 for grocery store shoplifting incidents in United States
items.x: WEST VIRGINIA (WTRF) — West Virginia had the ninth-highest rate of reported grocery store shoplifting incidents in the country, according to an analysis by H&P Law . The state recorded 6,350 incidents from 2021 through 2025, averaging 1,270 per year. That equals 71.64 incidents for every 100,000 residents. The analysis used FBI Crime Data Explorer figures and U.S. Census Bureau population estimates. West Virginia’s number of incidents rose 42.7% between the first and final years studied. Kentucky recorded a 25.4% increase during the same period. The state’s rate was 2.4 times Pennsylvania’s rate of 29.50 incidents per 100,000 people. West Virginia also ranked above Ohio at 61.52 and Virginia at 60.22. New Mexico ranked first with 156.53 incidents per 100,000 residents, more than twice West Virginia’s rate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: VSP: Man dies after striking VDOT contractor vehicle on I-64
items.x: YORK COUNTY, Va. (WAVY) A 52-year-old man died after striking a VDOT contractor vehicle Wednesday evening in York County, according to Virginia State Police. State police responded to I-64 East at mile marker 237 for a fatal two-vehicle crash at approximately 6:40 p.m. A preliminary investigation determined a VDOT contractor vehicle provided a safety net for a construction crew setting out warning signs for an overnight lane closure when it was crashed into by a 2025 Ford Mustang. The Mustang operator, 52-year-old Michael Ohman, of Newport News, suffered serious injuries and was taken to the hospital for treatment. He later died at the hospital. State police confirmed no VDOT contractors were harmed in the crash. The incident remains under investigation.

But, before you head into the woods, there is one very important thing to consider. "Is my gun ready?" The only way to tell is to fire it at a target to make sure the scope and gun are in synch, and that your aim is true. If not, you will need to make adjustments on the scope and possibly the gun. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. items.t: North Carolina flags to fly at half-staff in honor of civil rights icon Dolores Huerta
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. (WGHP) Governor Josh Stein ordered all U.S. and North Carolina flags at state facilities to be flown at half-staff from sunrise on Thursday until sunset Monday in honor of labor activist and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta . Huerta died on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, California. The 96-year old civil rights activist spent decades championing equal rights for women, immigrants and workers. She is widely remembered for cofounding the United Farm Workers of America in the mid-1960s. "Dolores Huerta made America a better place for workers and women, moving our nation forward," Stein said. "Let us honor her legacy by continuing to extend the promise of this nation to all who call it home. May her memory be a blessing."

items.t: 8 signs your anxiety is affecting your physical health
items.x: Anxiety and physical health are closely connected. When anxiety sticks around, it keeps your body’s fight or flight response switched on, releasing stress hormones like adrenaline and cortisol that affect your heart, breathing, digestion, muscles and sleep. Common signs that anxiety is taking a physical toll include a racing heart, shortness of breath, stomach problems, headaches, constant fatigue, dizziness, sweating and flare-ups of other health conditions. Most people expect anxiety to show up as worry. items.t: Constantly congested? 7 reasons your nose may always be blocked
items.x: If you are always congested, the cause is usually something other than a cold that never ends. Ear, nose and throat specialists say ongoing stuffiness is most often driven by allergies, chronic sinus inflammation, nasal polyps, a deviated septum, irritants in the air, non-allergic rhinitis or overuse of decongestant sprays. Congestion that lasts 12 weeks or longer is considered chronic and is worth a closer look. That 12-week mark matters more than most people realize. A blocked nose can wreck your sleep, your workouts and your focus. items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

When firefighters arrived, they found a badly damaged vehicle with Autumn trapped inside. It took several crews to cut her out with the Jaws of Life hydraulic rescue tools. Anchorage firefighter Jason Dolph said moose are particularly dangerous when they are hit at highway speeds. “Typically when a car strikes a moose, that moose becomes suspended in the air,”

items.t: Ukraine war continues despite Trump’s promise to end it
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The war in Ukraine has lasted more than four-and-a-half years, and fighting continues despite repeated efforts by President Donald Trump to end the conflict. Trump made a pledge on the campaign trail dozens of times during the last presidential campaign. “Before I even arrive at the Oval Office shortly after I win the presidency, I will have the horrible war between Russia and Ukraine settled,” Trump said at a July 7, 2023, rally in Council Bluffs, Iowa. “Somebody said, are you on Russia’s side? Are you on Ukraine’s side? You know what? The side — I want people to stop dying. That’s the side I’m on.” That campaign promise has not been fulfilled. Trump has met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy twice at the White House. items.t: We Walk the Line: Turning loss into a lifeline
items.x: (Editor’s note: This story discusses suicide. If you or a loved one needs help, call or text the Suicide Prevention Hotline at 988.) LANSING, Mich. ( Aging Untold ) — Members of the military and first responders run toward crisis and the repeated trauma can take a serious toll on mental health. A growing number of veterans and first responders are dying by suicide, struggling with the invisible wounds of service. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs estimates an average of 22 veterans take their own lives each day, and hundreds of first responders die by suicide annually. Two Michigan nonprofits are working together to help, providing free therapy and service dogs to veterans and first responders. For Tonya and Scott Shea, the mission is personal. items.t: ‘She just lit up the room’: Toddler dies after being hit by car at a pumpkin patch, family says
items.x: SEVIERVILLE, Tenn. ( WVLT /Gray News) - A Tennessee toddler died after being hit by a car at a pumpkin patch, according to her family. The family of 21-month-old Nyxailia Hinton said they want answers after she died Tuesday. The Sevier County Sheriff’s Office said she fell and was hit by a car driven by a family friend at a pumpkin patch. However, details have not been given about how or where she fell. “She just lit up the room,” said Peandra Hinton, the child’s mother. “If you were having a bad day, you see Zayla, she’s gonna turn it all around.” Hinton said her daughter was with a babysitter who took her to the pumpkin patch without permission. She said her daughter was with a group of people she did not know. Hinton rushed to the hospital, where her daughter died from her injuries Tuesday, according to the sheriff’s office. items.t: DOJ asks Washington state to set aside 400 voter ballots
items.x: SEATTLE (KPTV) — Federal authorities are asking Washington election officials to set aside ballots from more than 400 voters they suspect registered without U.S. citizenship. At a news conference Monday at the federal courthouse in Seattle, the U.S. Attorney’s Office alleged it identified 400 people who voted illegally in state and federal elections, accounting for roughly 1,500 cast ballots. The Trump administration sent a formal request to the Washington Secretary of State’s Office asking election workers to sequester ballots cast by those individuals until their citizenship status can be verified. “We are asking the state to set aside those ballots until we can confirm they are legal voters,” Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said during the briefing. items.t: Man gets stuck in storm drain while running from officers in Eugene
items.x: EUGENE, Ore. (KPTV) - A man became stuck in a storm drain while running from officers on Tuesday morning, according to the Eugene Police Department. Just before 10 a.m. on Oct. 27, officers were called to help city employees at Mattie Reynolds Park to remove a tent that was put up near Amazon Creek. The man inside the tent gave officers a fake name and pretended not to know how to get out of the tent, according to police. The man, identified by police as 32-year-old Tylor Robert Welty, then ripped a hole in the tent with his hands and dove into the creek. Officers followed Welty as he swam downstream. Police said he climbed out of the creek at one point and got into a storm drain under the pedestrian bridge at West 12th Avenue and Wallis Street. Police said Welty became stuck about 100 yards in the drain and was physically pulled out of the pipe. Welty was taken to a hospital and later b

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. Those household formation years are very expensive, so GenZer’s actually have more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even adjusted for inflation according to TransUnion.” For Gen Z, Rossm

items.t: Hillsboro gas station celebrates selling winning Megabucks ticket
items.x: HILLSBORO, Ore. (KPTV) - A 54-year-old lottery player won a $4.2 million Megabucks jackpot with a ticket bought at the Tanasbourne West Chevron. The ticket was purchased earlier this month. The winner has come forward but wishes to remain anonymous. The Chevron, located at 7499 Northeast Imbrie Drive, received a $42,000 bonus for selling the winning ticket. Store owner Aref Zghoul said some of the money will go to employees. Manny Martinez, the clerk who sold the ticket, will receive the largest bonus, Zghoul said. Zghoul said the rest of the money will go to a cancer foundation and a local youth charity. He said some will also go toward small repairs to his store.

items.t: ‘He’s a monster’: Convicted Tennessee murderer still on the run as authorities investigate Wisconsin bank robbery
items.x: LAKE COUNTY, Tenn. ( WMC /Gray News) - The manhunt for escaped Tennessee inmate Jacob Allen Morley continues and authorities are investigating a possible link in Wisconsin after a man robbed a bank at gunpoint there on Tuesday. Dane County authorities said the Bank of Deerfield was robbed just before it closed. A gunman walked in, demanded money, restrained two employees and left with cash. Nobody was hurt during the robbery. The gunman stole a Lincoln MKZ from the parking lot to get away. The car was later found unoccupied. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said it is aware of the robbery in Wisconsin, but has not confirmed it is linked to Morley. Morley escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex Monday. items.t: Providence Cancer Institute program supports breast cancer patients beyond treatment
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - An emerging program at Providence Cancer Institute is supporting breast cancer patients through all aspects of their journey, with the aim of helping them live as full a life as possible. The program is called the Providence “Survivorship Program.” It is designed to help patients beyond surgery and treatment. One service offered through the program is a sound bath. The sound bath is a meditative experience that guides breast cancer patients away from fear and worry and into a less stressful space. “It helps create a soothing environment for the body that it’s like, oh, that’s what it feels like to feel grounded or settled,” said Michelle Ferretti, an oncology social worker. items.t: Man seriously hurt in SE Portland shooting
items.x: PORTLAND, Ore. (KPTV) - The Portland Police Bureau is investigating a shooting that happened in the Richmond neighborhood Wednesday night. At about 10:14 p.m., officers responded to a shooting near Southeast 35th Place and Southeast Division Street. Officers arrived to the scene and found a man who had been shot. The victim was taken to a hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries. Police said officers found some casings at the scene. No arrests have been made at this time, and a description of the suspect was not released. Anyone with information about the shooting should contact Portland police.

items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: TVF&R: Downed power lines fall onto SUV, shut down Hwy 26 overnight
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - Downed power lines led to an hours-long closure on Highway 26 overnight. Tualatin Valley Fire & Rescue said people near Murray Boulevard called 911 to report they heard an explosion and believed a transformer blew. TVF&R said power lines fell across Highway 26, with some lines landing on and around a black Bronco. The driver in the Bronco eventually drove over the lines, even though TVF&R said they were advised not to do that. All lanes of Highway 26 were closed at Murray Boulevard while Portland General Electric crews worked to repair the lines. The highway was reopened just after 5:30 a.m.

items.t: InvestigateTV+: Tracking the trackers
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — As the number of cameras capturing vehicle information multiplies, so do concerns of privacy for everyday people. InvestigateTV+ explores what can happen when the tool is misused and meet one man on a mission to track every police camera in the country. Plus, four-legged companions jump into action to help heal our heroes. We share the recent gift bringing military members support in the form of service animals. Tracking the trackers Flock Safety says its cameras don’t track people. But the company’s own training videos show police using the system to track suspects “from location to location to location.” And some of its cameras are designed to follow people as they walk. “And they quite literally use AI to zoom in and follow you around whether you’re a person of interest or not,” said Benn Jordan , a security researcher who found dozens of Flock cameras streaming op

items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. Barbershop quartets have been around for more than a century. Though they can be found all over the world, ties to New Orleans are strong. “It really is

items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. items.t: Tennessee governor suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will stay the same after failed execution
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WSMV /Gray News) — Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee said he suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will remain the same following her failed execution last month, unless the courts determine otherwise. Crash location and road closure The Yamhill County Sheriff’s Office said the crash was reported around 2:15 p.m. near Lafayette Highway and Southeast Stringtown Road. The crash scene is near McMinnville Municipal Airport, southeast of McMinnville. Aircraft involved The two helicopters were identified as an Airbus Helicopters AS350B2 and a Robinson R22, according to the NTSB. items.t: Flags lowered in honor of late deputy
items.x: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) – West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey on Thursday ordered flags at the Capitol Complex and all state buildings in Logan County to fly at half-staff Friday in honor of the late Deputy Caden Mullins. The Logan County Sheriff’s Office deputy is set to be laid to rest Friday after being killed in a crash involving a coal truck on Oct. 24. Mullins was a Logan County native and a graduate of Man High School.

items.t: Charleston parks see improvements as residents enjoy fall weather
items.x: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) - Even as temperatures dip, Charleston residents are still enjoying the outdoors as crews work to improve parks and recreation facilities across the city. John Barth, a longtime Cato Park visitor, said the park gives him a safe place to stay active. “It’s safe. That’s the main thing. I walk in the day, the night, in the morning — whenever I can get out and be healthy,” Barth said. Cato Park is among the facilities seeing improvements. According to a post from the city of Charleston, blacktop work is underway near the park’s maintenance building. Barth said he has lived in the area for most of his life and appreciates the work that goes into maintaining the park. “Makes me feel good. Real good. Like, I’ve lived here most of my life. I think I was 10 years old when we moved in here, and they just keep providing. It goes down, but they always keep it clean. The city

items.t: Trick-or-treat celebrated at Safety Town
items.x: HUNTINGTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) - Safety remains a priority during the Halloween season, and Thursday’s trick-or-treat event at Safety Town combined that reminder with a fun evening for the family. Huntington Police Department and more than 50 venders and organizations lined the streets of Safety Town to pass out candy to a crowd of costumed kids and their families. One person passing out candy said this type of event is good for the community. “It’s such a great, safe place that people know that they can bring their kids and they don’t have to worry about cars running them down and all kinds of crazy things happening,” Louise Holmes with Roll-A-Rama Skate Center said. “We love doing this. we love being out in the community, and we love Halloween.“ Head to the trick-or-treat tab on WSAZ.com for times and locations across the region.

items.t: A neighborhood scare: Midvale Haunt shows off ‘The Experiment’
items.x: HUNTINGTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) - For those looking for a thrill before Halloween, Midvale Haunt is bringing the sights and frights to its front yard. This year’s theme is The Experiment , based on Frankenstein. Visitors can even control the scares by pressing buttons at the bottom of the hill or texting “SCARE” from your car to trigger the show. The homemade attraction can be found on Midvale Drive. The folks at Midvale Haunt will also be passing out candy on Halloween for trick or treat. A full list of trick-or-treat times and locations can be found on WSAZ.com.

items.t: New Cabell County clerk sworn in
items.x: CABELL COUNTY, W.Va. (WSAZ) – Cabell County has a new clerk. Danne Vance was sworn in Thursday at the Cabell County Courthouse in Huntington. Vance replaces Scott Caserta, who recently retired. Vance previously served as a magistrate judge.

items.t: Midterm candidates say they are winning voters across party lines
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Some midterm election candidates have recently been promoting their ability to win over voters from across party lines but experts say it may not be enough to change outcomes in November. In recent weeks, Democratic candidates in several states have promoted endorsements from Republican officials and voters. In Alaska, Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski endorsed Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins on Tuesday. In Kansas, two former Republican governors, Bill Graves and Mike Hayden, announced in September and October that they are backing Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Adam Hamilton. In Texas, the campaign for Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico said that over two dozen former GOP officials have endorsed Talarico. items.t: Spooky Halloween Haven
items.x: WAYNE COUNTY, W.Va. (WSAZ) - It’s time for All Hallows Eve when ghosts, ghouls and witches come out to prey on the weak and weary! For kids of all ages, it’s one of the best holidays of the entire year. To get you ready for trick-or-treat, Tony Cavalier found one haunted house out in Wayne Country where the frights come aplenty -- even during the day!

items.t: Decision 2026 | Mason County Board of Education, explained
items.x: MASON COUNTY, W.Va. (WSAZ) - The Mason County Board of Education is asking county voters for the same tax levy that has been on the books for more than 70 years. But this year, there’s nearly $100 million more dollars on the line with that vote. The ballot measure, if passed, is expected to bring in nearly $10 million per year in property taxes, using the same levy rates as have been passed for years. But according to the state Treasurer’s Office, the levy could bring in an extra $90 million because of the two data centers currently being built in the county. “The only money the Board of Education can get, any Board of Education can get, with respect to these data centers, is if they have an excess levy in the county,” Pack previously explained to WSAZ. “If the excess levy goes away, then the Board of Education does not get any of the money, with respect to the data centers.” If the levy

items.t: Youth sports coach sentenced for sexually assaulting 12-year-old girl he coached
items.x: PEORIA, Ill. ( 25News Now /Gray News) - A youth sports coach has been sentenced to 26 years in prison for sexually assaulting a 12-year-old girl he coached. Aydan Trueblood was sentenced Wednesday after pleading guilty to predatory criminal sexual assault in August, according to the Peoria County State’s Attorney’s Office. Assistant State’s Attorney Dave Gast argued for the 30-year maximum permitted under the plea agreement, emphasizing the victim’s age. Chief Judge Katherine Gorman acknowledged Trueblood’s lack of criminal history but said he needed to take accountability for his actions. “This is the nightmare of every parent with a daughter in a sport,” Gast said. Bartonville Police received a tip on Nov. 9 that Trueblood had behaved inappropriately with the victim. items.t: Record number of female candidates in 2026 midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections are set to be historic. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. This year, an increase in candidates nationwide has led more women to run for office, with a historic number of women having been nominated ahead of the Nov. 3 election. “We have a record number of women running for the House overall, a record number of Democratic women running. That’s also true when we look at gubernatorial contests,” Dittmar said. Dittmar said the trend gives the upcoming 120th Congress a chance to be

items.t: Man convicted of shooting woman in the head after argument
items.x: BEAUFORT, S.C. ( WCSC /Gray News) — A man is expected to spend two decades behind bars for shooting a woman in the head after a verbal argument in an apartment parking lot in 2023. This week, Bernard “Berney” Garvin Jr., 35, was found guilty of attempted murder and possession of a weapon during the commission of a violent crime. Deputies with the Beaufort County Sheriff’s Office responded to reports of a shooting at the Hilton Head Gardens apartment complex in June of that year. Upon arrival, they reported finding a pool of blood, spent shell casings on the pavement and bullet damage on a parked minivan. Further investigation revealed that a woman was grazed in the head by a bullet after she argued with Garvin before arriving at the complex. items.t: 2026 midterms set new record for political ad spending
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. items.t: 71-year-old grandmother missing after going on walk more than 3 weeks ago, police say
items.x: (Gray News) - A 71-year-old New Jersey woman went for a walk more than three weeks ago and hasn’t been seen since. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. Franklin Township police and the family are urging residents to check doorbell and security cameras for possible sightings. Anyone with information is asked to call the Franklin Township Police Department at 732-873-2300.

items.t: Enslow Park Bridge weight limit reduced to nine tons
items.x: HUNTINGTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) - The weight limit on the Enslow Park Bridge has dropped from 33 tons to nine tons. Students who live in the Enslow Park neighborhood now have to go to the end of the road to catch the school bus instead of being picked up and dropped off at home. Cabell County Schools said buses 8-76, 7-69 and 7-99 are not able to cross the bridge. Until the bridge is replaced, the bus will pick up and drop off students at the end of the bridge. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

(WSAZ) - Kentucky State Police says a couple has been arrested after the discovery of a large amount of suspected illegal drugs at a residence in the Elkhorn City community on Tuesday. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said.
