Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. items.t: Record number of female candidates in 2026 midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections are set to be historic. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. items.t: 2026 midterms set new record for political ad spending
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. items.x: (Gray News) - A 71-year-old New Jersey woman went for a walk more than three weeks ago and hasn’t been seen since. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. items.t: 79-year-old man killed after collision with fire truck
items.x: WICHITA, Kan. ( KWCH /Gray News) - A 79-year-old man was killed in a crash involving a fire truck. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. The crash caused the vehicles to hit another vehicle, a black Dodge Ram. The 79-year-old man died at the hospital. He was identified by police as James Mattson of Wichita. The driver of the Dodge Ram was not hurt, nor were the four firefighters inside the fire truck. The WPD Critical Accident Team will investigate the crash.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. Stewart’s diagnoses had not been previously disclosed. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the “X-Men” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation” series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of “A Christmas Carol” and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” and Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. As an infant, Trae Caster suffered severe, permanent brain damage from shaken baby syndrome caused by a caregiver. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

But when a big vote happens and it’s a tie, this person decides yay or nay. That’s because the lieutenant governor is president of the Texas Senate, according to the Texas Constitution and the Texas Senate. The office picks Senate committee members and chairs and co-chairs boards that shape the state budget, plus coordinates public education policy and funding, according to the Office of the Lieutenant Governor and the Texas Senate. Should the governor not be able to serve, temporarily or permanently, the lieutenant governor steps in and fills the role until the chief returns or until the elected term ends, according to the Texas Constitution. The governor is elected by citizens every four years, according to the Office of the Texas Governor. The governor must be at least 30 years old and a resident of Texas for the five years immediately before the election. The governor makes policy recommendations that lawmakers in the state House and Senate may sponsor and introduce as bills. The governor also appoints the secretary of state, as well as members of boards and commissions who oversee the heads of state agencies and departments. Constitutional and statutory duties include signing or vetoing bills passed by the Legislature, serving as commander-in-chief of the state’s military forces and convening special sessions of the Legislature for specific purposes, according to the Office of the Texas Governor. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: Trump slams Peltola campaign over two Sullivans on Alaska ballot
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - President Donald Trump and Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska) are accusing Democrats of intentionally trying to confuse Alaska voters, after two candidates named Dan Sullivan appeared on the state’s midterm election ballot for U.S. Senate. Trump is among several Republicans criticizing Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola, accusing her of perpetuating a fraud on Alaska voters. The New York Times reported Wednesday that campaign staffers for Peltola, a former Alaska congresswoman now running for the U.S. Senate, tried to recruit a candidate with the same name as Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. The effort is not illegal. However, the reports have led Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a Republican, to order an investigation into alleged election manipulation. Trump commented on the controversy Thursday before leaving for South Carolina. “So nobody’s going to know what to do.

items.t: Baby dies after 15-year-old girl gives birth at elementary school, reports say
items.x: CHICAGO — Authorities are reportedly investigating the death of a baby after a teen girl gave birth at an elementary school in the Chicago area on Wednesday. Chicago police shared that a 15-year-old girl gave birth at Aldridge Elementary School on East 131st Street, but the baby was pronounced dead at the scene. WLS reports that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office listed the location of the death as 630 E. 131st St. in Chicago, which is the address for Aldridge Elementary School. The teen girl was reportedly in good condition when taken to an area hospital for treatment. Officials from the elementary school did not immediately comment on the situation, WGN reported.

The Longborough dock is currently owned by the Longborough Homeowners Association, so it’s closed off to the public and nearby neighbors in the upper peninsula. The City of Charleston’s Real Estate Committee approved a motion to buy a portion of the land, including a dock, for $1 million. Mayor William Cogswell said this is a way to bring a public waterway for the Upper Peninsula to enjoy. “While there was a disagreement on this, this is a compromise to allow people to have access. It’s not just crabbing. I mean, you can launch a kayak from the crabbing dock. I mean, you can paddle board from it. items.t: 16-year-old killed in tractor crash with semi-truck, officials say
items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. Crash reports showed this was the second farm equipment crash that happened in Audubon County on Sunday. The other crash left a pickup truck driver with serious injuries after it crashed head-on with a combine.

items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. items.x: (Gray News) - Almost 340,000 space heaters are under recall throughout the United States due to the risk of fire and burns. DREO space heaters model DR-HSH015 were placed under recall on Oct. 29, the Consumer Product Safety Commission reported. About 338,800 units were affected, with an additional 36,300 sold in Canada. items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. Stewart’s diagnoses had not been previously disclosed. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the “X-Men” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation” series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of “A Christmas Carol” and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” and Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen. items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we examine the subtle, easily overlooked early warning signs of Parkinson’s disease and discuss when to talk with a physician. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. items.t: Hornets coach Charles Lee benches Naz Reid at halftime for failing to meet team standards
items.x: DETROIT (AP) — Hornets forward Naz Reid was benched for the second half of Charlotte’s loss Wednesday night at Detroit for failing to meet coach Charles Lee’s standards. “Unfortunately, Naz didn’t meet our standards in the first half, and at halftime we made the decision that he wouldn’t play in the second half,” Lee said. “But I look forward to him meeting those standards come next game.” Lee did not specify the standards Reid failed to meet. The Hornets, who play Friday night at Washington, dealt star point LaMelo Ball to Minnesota in the offseason, and Reid came to Charlotte in the deal. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. items.t: Record number of female candidates in 2026 midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections are set to be historic. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. This year, an increase in candidates nationwide has led more women to run for office, with a historic number of women having been nominated ahead of the Nov. 3 election. “We have a record number of women running for the House overall, a record number of Democratic women running. items.t: 2026 midterms set new record for political ad spending
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: Record number of female candidates in 2026 midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections are set to be historic. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. items.t: 2026 midterms set new record for political ad spending
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. Anyone with information is asked to call the Franklin Township Police Department at 732-873-2300.

items.t: Experts share tips for easing mental health effects of the time change
items.x: PRINCETON, W.Va. (WVVA) - Clocks fall back one hour at 2 a.m. this Sunday as daylight saving time ends. Mental health experts say preparing now can help people prone to seasonal depression. For some people, the time change means one more hour of sleep. For others, it is the beginning of seasonal depression. Why the time change affects mood Nearly 40% of Americans report that their mood worsens during the winter months each year. Days become shorter, and people receive more light in the morning and less sun in the evening. The abruptness of the time change tends to affect people the most. Dr. Alina Vrincin-Hamm, a psychiatrist with Southern Highlands, said the change disrupts daily routines. “So, all of the sudden, we’ll notice on Sunday that it gets dark a whole hour earlier. And that sudden change is disruptive to our sleep schedules, our mood, and our energy,” Vrincin-Hamm said. Prepar

items.t: 79-year-old man killed after collision with fire truck
items.x: WICHITA, Kan. ( KWCH /Gray News) - A 79-year-old man was killed in a crash involving a fire truck. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. The crash caused the vehicles to hit another vehicle, a black Dodge Ram. The 79-year-old man died at the hospital. He was identified by police as James Mattson of Wichita. The driver of the Dodge Ram was not hurt, nor were the four firefighters inside the fire truck. The WPD Critical Accident Team will investigate the crash.

items.t: Bluefield State University introduces interim president Ronald Johnson
items.x: BLUEFIELD, W.Va. (WVVA) - Bluefield State University introduced Ronald Johnson as its interim president Thursday. Johnson previously held positions as interim president at Tennessee State and Kentucky State. He said he wants to understand the people at Bluefield State University and what they need to accomplish to achieve success for students. “My role is to get this institution on a track so that when the permanent president comes in, the permanent president can then actually take this institution and now move it in terms of really lift off,” Johnson said. “So, if you don’t have a foundation, you can’t lift off.” Johnson said he plans to meet people and understand what roadblocks they are facing so the university can improve and grow overall. Johnson did not graduate from Bluefield State University. He said students can look at him and see what future success could look like.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. According to Stone, the collision occurred when her daughter Autumn was driving home and a moose appeared in the roadway. Stone said she does not believe her daughter had any time to brake. When firefighters arrived, they found a badly damaged vehicle with Autumn trapped inside. It took several crews to cut her out with the Jaws of Life hydraulic rescue tools. items.t: Ukraine war continues despite Trump’s promise to end it
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The war in Ukraine has lasted more than four-and-a-half years, and fighting continues despite repeated efforts by President Donald Trump to end the conflict. Trump made a pledge on the campaign trail dozens of times during the last presidential campaign. “Before I even arrive at the Oval Office shortly after I win the presidency, I will have the horrible war between Russia and Ukraine settled,” Trump said at a July 7, 2023, rally in Council Bluffs, Iowa. “Somebody said, are you on Russia’s side? Are you on Ukraine’s side? You know what? The side — I want people to stop dying. That’s the side I’m on.” That campaign promise has not been fulfilled. Trump has met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy twice at the White House. items.t: West Virginia experiencing increase in Salmonella Typhimurium cases
items.x: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WVVA) – The West Virginia Department of Health (WVDH) is investigating an outbreak of Salmonella Typhimurium. The outbreak started in early September, and 41 cases have been reported. Patients range in age from three to 54 years and five have been hospitalized. A common source has not been identified and exposures are under investigation. None of the cases outside West Virginia have been linked to this outbreak, indicating a localized event. To identify the source, timely reporting and specimen submission are essential. Collaboration between healthcare providers, laboratories and public health for Salmonella surveillance is vital in these cases. Salmonella Typhimurium is one of the most reported Salmonella serotypes in the U.S. It is acquired primarily through consuming contaminated food or water and encountering infected animals and their environments. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Hospice of Southern West Virginia to host lunch and tours for first responders
items.x: BECKLEY, W.Va. (WVVA) – Hospice of Southern West Virginia (HSWV) will welcome local first responders to its campus for a lunch and tours in recognition of National First Responders Day. The event will take place on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. at Bowers Hospice House, located at 454 Cranberry Drive in Beckley. First Responders can enjoy lunch, connect with members of the Hospice of Southern West Virginia and learn more about the care that they provide to the region. Guests can also take an informal tour of the campus, including Bowers Hospice House, and see the environment where hospice care is provided. “There is no formal program,” said Tommy Redden, Chief Operating Officer, HSWV. “This is simply an opportunity to share a meal, have a conversation, see our facilities and build relationships with the first responders who serve our communities every day.”

items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections are set to be historic. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. items.t: 2026 midterms set new record for political ad spending
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. items.t: 71-year-old grandmother missing after going on walk more than 3 weeks ago, police say
items.x: (Gray News) - A 71-year-old New Jersey woman went for a walk more than three weeks ago and hasn’t been seen since. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. Franklin Township police and the family are urging residents to check doorbell and security cameras for possible sightings. Anyone with information is asked to call the Franklin Township Police Department at 732-873-2300.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. Jones was born in Portland, Oregon, on Feb. 19, 1953. He played college football at Oregon, Hawaii and Portland State. At Portland State, he played under Mouse Davis, the innovator of the run-and-shoot offense, which Jones himself would later make famous. He played 17 games at quarterback for the Falcons between 1977 and 1981, starting five games. The Falcons went 1-4 in his starts and Jones finished his career with 923 yards, three touchdowns and seven interceptions. He then played for the Canadian Football League’s Toronto Argonauts in 1982 before beginning a coaching career. items.t: Juvenile dies in Cobb County car crash, police say
items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — A child died in a Cobb County car crash on Wednesday night, according to police. At around 7:30 p.m., Cobb County police were called to the intersection of Macland Road and Ernest Barrett Parkway in unincorporated Marietta. The juvenile, who has not been identified, was pronounced dead at the scene. Investigators believe a red 2016 Kia Forte driven by a 39-year-old from Powder Springs and occupied by a juvenile was on Macland Road. While turning left onto Ernest Barrett Parkway, the Kia entered the path of a blue 2019 Chevrolet Silverado, according to police. The Chevrolet hit the Kia’s right side and rolled over onto its roof. Its driver, a 25-year-old from Powder Springs, was taken to the hospital, where he is expected to recover. The Kia’s driver wasn’t hurt. Police have not identified the underage victim. The incident is still under investigation.

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: What Georgia’s handwritten voter list at check-in is and isn’t
items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — When you check in to vote, you may see poll workers handwriting your name on a numbered sheet. That sheet is called a “Numbered List of Voters.” Under State Election Board Rule 183-1-12-.02, it is defined as numbered sheets where workers enter each voter’s name at the time and in the order voters receive ballots. Full election results here Counties already check voters in electronically. The handwritten list creates a paper record of the same event, who appeared to vote , that can be used to audit participation counts. Election officials say the list tracks that you voted, not how you voted. It does not record the choices marked on your secret ballot. Full election day coverage from Atlanta News First Under Georgia Code § 21-2-225, voter lists showing who voted are available for public inspection. Ballot choices remain secret under law. items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — Before you ever check in to vote, the equipment you’ll use is already tracked on paper through what election officials call chain of custody. Under State Election Board Rules in Chapter 183-1-12, counties must securely store and transport ballot markers and scanners, maintain numbered seals on the machines with seal numbers on file, and complete chain-of-custody forms when equipment and voted ballots are transferred. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

A growing number of veterans and first responders are dying by suicide, struggling with the invisible wounds of service. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs estimates an average of 22 veterans take their own lives each day, and hundreds of first responders die by suicide annually. Two Michigan nonprofits are working together to help, providing free therapy and service dogs to veterans and first responders. For Tonya and Scott Shea, the mission is personal. items.t: ‘She just lit up the room’: Toddler dies after being hit by car at a pumpkin patch, family says
items.x: SEVIERVILLE, Tenn. ( WVLT /Gray News) - A Tennessee toddler died after being hit by a car at a pumpkin patch, according to her family. The family of 21-month-old Nyxailia Hinton said they want answers after she died Tuesday. The Sevier County Sheriff’s Office said she fell and was hit by a car driven by a family friend at a pumpkin patch. However, details have not been given about how or where she fell. “She just lit up the room,” said Peandra Hinton, the child’s mother. “If you were having a bad day, you see Zayla, she’s gonna turn it all around.” Hinton said her daughter was with a babysitter who took her to the pumpkin patch without permission. She said her daughter was with a group of people she did not know. Hinton rushed to the hospital, where her daughter died from her injuries Tuesday, according to the sheriff’s office. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. Those household formation years are very expensive, so GenZer’s actually have more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even adjusted for inflation according to TransUnion.” For Gen Z, Rossm

items.t: FIRST ALERT: Remembering the rare Halloween Hurricane of 1899
items.x: MYRTLE BEACH, SC (WMBF) — Halloween is usually associated with pumpkins, candy, and cool fall nights. But more than a century ago, Halloween along the Carolina coast brought something much more frightening: a powerful hurricane. HALLOWEEN HURRICANE TRACK The year was 1899, and the ninth storm of the Atlantic hurricane season was making its way toward the Carolinas. The storm became a hurricane on October 28th before making landfall in Cuba a day later. By October 30th, it had strengthened into a Category 2 hurricane, striking the Grand Bahama Island with sustained winds of 110 miles per hour. But the storm wasn’t finished. Early on Halloween morning, around 5 a.m., the hurricane made its final landfall near what we now know as Myrtle Beach, with sustained winds estimated at 105 miles per hour. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. InvestigateTV+ explores what can happen when the tool is misused and meet one man on a mission to track every police camera in the country. Plus, four-legged companions jump into action to help heal our heroes. We share the recent gift bringing military members support in the form of service animals. But the company’s own training videos show police using the system to track suspects “from location to location to location.” And some of its cameras are designed to follow people as they walk. “And they quite literally use AI to zoom in and follow you around whether you’re a person of interest or not,” said Benn Jordan , a security researcher who found dozens of Flock cameras streaming op

items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. items.x: CONWAY, SC (WMBF) - A man was sentenced to 10 years in prison for a fentanyl charge in Conway. Edmund Leviner, 34, of Conway pleaded guilty to second-offense possession with intent to distribute fentanyl in Conway on Oct. 20. items.t: UMary women’s soccer claims first NSIC regular-season title
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D (KFYR) - The University of Mary women’s soccer team made program history, defeating Highway 83 rival Minot State 4-1 in its regular-season finale to earn a share of its first Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference championship. The Marauders finished conference play 12-1-2, sharing the title with Minnesota State Mankato. Dina Polanco led the way with two goals, opening the scoring on a penalty kick and added her 20th goal of the season in the 56th minute. Harlee Peltz sealed the victory with a header six minutes later. UMary enters the postseason unbeaten in its last 13 games. items.t: Chair, vice chair of North Dakota Development Fund resign
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D. (KMOT/KFYR) – The chair and vice chair of a state fund that’s come under financial scrutiny in recent weeks have resigned. A spokesperson for Gov. Kelly Armstrong’s office confirmed that Jim Albrecht and Rob Lindberg submitted their resignations with the North Dakota Development Fund. The spokesperson could not specify when their resignations were effective, and said the governor did not have further comment at this time. There wasn’t a reason provided for their resignations. The commission’s inquiry does not establish that an ethics violation has occurred. This is a developing story. Stay with Your News Leader for updates.

items.t: Neighbors charged in meth trafficking case
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - Police in Bismarck have arrested three people following a major drug bust uncovering more than three pounds of methamphetamine. According to court documents, investigators executed a federal search warrant Tuesday at an apartment building on North 2nd Street. Inside, officers seized over 1,400 grams of meth, along with prescription pills, digital scales, heat-sealing equipment and a large amount of cash. Clarence Taylor, Sandra Schulte and Otis Lewis face charges of conspiracy and possession of methamphetamine with intent to deliver. items.t: Sip and Swirl opens in Bismarck
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - A new business in Bismarck is giving people a place to get creative and grab a drink as the colder weather sets in. Sip and Swirl combines paint-your-own pottery with a custom soda bar. Visitors can walk in without an appointment, choose from dozens of pieces ranging from $10 to $50, and pick their paint style, either taking their finished project home that day or leaving it to be fired in a kiln. “It was kind of something that merged inside my head. I thought, ‘oh, you know, custom sodas are becoming really big.’ That would be fun. But also, I know in Minot, they have a really cool pottery painting place,” owner Tina Kitzman said. “So I thought, let’s combine the two.” While walk-ins are welcome for general painting, private party rooms for birthdays and office gatherings can be booked online here .

items.t: Jeannette Myhre Elementary hosts first Halloween Bash
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - Zombies and ghouls took the dance floor Thursday at a Bismarck school. Students and families gathered at Jeannette Myhre Elementary for the school’s first ever Halloween Bash. It partnered with United Way to host the event. Volunteers with Women United served food at the event, including first lady Kjersti Armstrong. “We’ve never done this before, and we just wanted to do something different. We decided not to have costumes during the day because we wanted our parents and their parents and families to be involved in it. And we thought ‘what more could we do’?” Dr. Kimberly Herman said, the school’s principal. Dr. Herman says they hope to bring the Halloween Bash back for another year. Their next event is their Thanksgiving Meal, where the school provides meals to the community.

items.t: Record number of female candidates in 2026 midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections are set to be historic. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. items.t: SERVPRO Athlete of the Week: Drake-Anamoose’s Mariah Mack
items.x: DRAKE, N.D. (KMOT) - Drake-Anamoose volleyball is the number one seed in the Class B District 6 tournament. The Raiders went 9-0 in regular season district play, winning 27 sets while dropping only four. Leading the charge is a senior outside hitter who has reached career milestones on both offense and defense. items.t: Man convicted of shooting woman in the head after argument

With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. items.t: Aggie Foundation helping First District Health Unit expand healthcare services
items.x: MINOT, N.D. (KMOT) – A group of friends that came together 14 years ago are still working together to make communities better. Their latest donation from their non-profit will help people who have trouble with their feet. Sadie Lynn reports on what the donation means for those receiving the gift and those who donated it. First District Health Unit (FDHU) is expanding its foot care services at its Minot office. The donation from the Aggie Foundation will help fund an autoclave, a machine that sterilizes foot care equipment. “It’s just one of the tools that, you know, allows us to provide safe services to our clients because it cleans the tools and things that the nurses use,” Holly Brekhus said, FDHU Executive Director. items.t: 71-year-old grandmother missing after going on walk more than 3 weeks ago, police say
items.x: (Gray News) - A 71-year-old New Jersey woman went for a walk more than three weeks ago and hasn’t been seen since. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. Franklin Township police and the family are urging residents to check doorbell and security cameras for possible sightings. Anyone with information is asked to call the Franklin Township Police Department at 732-873-2300.

The fund helps new and expanding North Dakota businesses obtain financing they may not be able to secure through traditional lenders. items.t: Bismarck opens bids for new south-side fire station
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - Bismarck’s sixth fire station is moving closer to construction, with a location chosen to help crews reach emergencies in the south part of the city faster. The project went out for bids Thursday. The station is planned for Calypso Drive, a location determined by response data and studies of the area’s needs, according to Luke Teagle, deputy chief at the Bismarck Fire Department. Crews currently take around six minutes to reach those areas. The goal is to bring that response time below four and a half minutes. “And it allows us, again, like I said earlier, to get into just that whole area a lot quicker,” Teagle said. “Has the firefighters working closer to the citizens. Children as young as 5 have enjoyed the haunted house. items.t: 79-year-old man killed after collision with fire truck
items.x: WICHITA, Kan. ( KWCH /Gray News) - A 79-year-old man was killed in a crash involving a fire truck. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. The crash caused the vehicles to hit another vehicle, a black Dodge Ram. The 79-year-old man died at the hospital. He was identified by police as James Mattson of Wichita. The driver of the Dodge Ram was not hurt, nor were the four firefighters inside the fire truck. The WPD Critical Accident Team will investigate the crash.

items.t: We The People: Historical photograph of Lincoln on display
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - A historical picture of the 16th President of the United States is returning to the “Land of Lincoln.” The photograph of Abraham Lincoln - which is more than 160 years old - was unveiled at the Peoria Riverfront Museum. Officials said the image was taken while Lincoln was getting ready to debate Stephen Douglas in U.S. Senate race. A photographer by the name of Roderick Cole requested a snap-shot and Lincoln agreed. The museum’s chief curator said this is the only known picture of Lincoln that was taken in Peoria. The picture was found in New York City, and then brought to Peoria.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

Chicago police shared that a 15-year-old girl gave birth at Aldridge Elementary School on East 131st Street, but the baby was pronounced dead at the scene. WLS reports that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office listed the location of the death as 630 E. 131st St. in Chicago, which is the address for Aldridge Elementary School. items.t: 16-year-old killed in tractor crash with semi-truck, officials say
items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. Crash reports showed this was the second farm equipment crash that happened in Audubon County on Sunday. items.t: Why so many banks? Why North Dakota has many places to bank

According to the president and CEO of the North Dakota Bankers Association, Rick Clayburgh, a lot of that has to do with regulatory and economic pressures. These are locations that can belong to banks headquartered here or somewhere else. “I think it’s more unique in rural America more than anything. items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide

Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

(WKYT) - It is Bat Week in Kentucky, with the Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services celebrating the benefits of having bats around and what to do if you come across one. Bats are flying mammals commonly associated with Halloween and vampires, but the bats in Kentucky do not feed on blood. Bats eat insects. Michaela Rogers, a wildlife biologist with the Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife, said all the state’s bats are insectivorous, meaning they eat bugs. “One of the main things that people think of them for is a really natural pest control,” Rogers said. “They go out every evening, and they’re going to be eating their weight in insects every single night, so that not only helps us with the bugs around our yards that we may not like as much, but also farmers with pest controls, that sort of thing.” Where bats live There are 15 bat species native to Kentucky.

items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide

items.t: 71-year-old grandmother missing after going on walk more than 3 weeks ago, police say
items.x: (Gray News) - A 71-year-old New Jersey woman went for a walk more than three weeks ago and hasn’t been seen since. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. Franklin Township police and the family are urging residents to check doorbell and security cameras for possible sightings. Anyone with information is asked to call the Franklin Township Police Department at 732-873-2300.

items.t: Midlands parents, poison center share Halloween safety tips
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - Thousands of children across the Midlands will go trick-or-treating this weekend, and experts at the Palmetto Poison Center said some Halloween risks can be prevented. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission said more than 3,000 Halloween-related injuries are treated in emergency rooms each year. Eat before trick-or-treating Experts at the Palmetto Poison Center said exposures to irritating chemicals and unchecked candy are common calls on Halloween night. They recommend families eat a meal before heading out so hungry children do not graze on the go. items.t: 79-year-old man killed after collision with fire truck
items.x: WICHITA, Kan. ( KWCH /Gray News) - A 79-year-old man was killed in a crash involving a fire truck. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. The crash caused the vehicles to hit another vehicle, a black Dodge Ram. The 79-year-old man died at the hospital. He was identified by police as James Mattson of Wichita. The driver of the Dodge Ram was not hurt, nor were the four firefighters inside the fire truck. The WPD Critical Accident Team will investigate the crash.
