items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: Baby dies after 15-year-old girl gives birth at elementary school, reports say
items.x: CHICAGO — Authorities are reportedly investigating the death of a baby after a teen girl gave birth at an elementary school in the Chicago area on Wednesday. Chicago police shared that a 15-year-old girl gave birth at Aldridge Elementary School on East 131st Street, but the baby was pronounced dead at the scene. WLS reports that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office listed the location of the death as 630 E. 131st St. in Chicago, which is the address for Aldridge Elementary School. The teen girl was reportedly in good condition when taken to an area hospital for treatment. Officials from the elementary school did not immediately comment on the situation, WGN reported.

items.t: 16-year-old killed in tractor crash with semi-truck, officials say
items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. Crash reports showed this was the second farm equipment crash that happened in Audubon County on Sunday. The other crash left a pickup truck driver with serious injuries after it crashed head-on with a combine.

items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. DREO space heaters model DR-HSH015 were placed under recall on Oct. 29, the Consumer Product Safety Commission reported. About 338,800 units were affected, with an additional 36,300 sold in Canada. items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. Stewart’s diagnoses had not been previously disclosed. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the “X-Men” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation” series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of “A Christmas Carol” and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” and Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: ‘He’s a monster’: Convicted Tennessee murderer still on the run as authorities investigate Wisconsin bank robbery
items.x: LAKE COUNTY, Tenn. ( WMC /Gray News) - The manhunt for escaped Tennessee inmate Jacob Allen Morley continues and authorities are investigating a possible link in Wisconsin after a man robbed a bank at gunpoint there on Tuesday. Dane County authorities said the Bank of Deerfield was robbed just before it closed. A gunman walked in, demanded money, restrained two employees and left with cash. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

( WDRB+WAVE /Gray News) — A Kentucky woman’s designated caretaker was arrested after allegedly recording an incident in which her 92-year-old husband allegedly tried to suffocate her instead of helping the victim. Bert Morris, 92, was charged Wednesday with attempted murder and first-degree strangulation. According to Morris’ arrest citation, Louisville Metro Police officers responded to a senior living center after a report of a domestic violence incident. items.t: Space heaters under recall after units reportedly catch fire
items.x: (Gray News) - Almost 340,000 space heaters are under recall throughout the United States due to the risk of fire and burns. DREO space heaters model DR-HSH015 were placed under recall on Oct. 29, the Consumer Product Safety Commission reported. About 338,800 units were affected, with an additional 36,300 sold in Canada. They were sold directly through DREO and other sites like Best Buy and Home Depot between Sept. 2025 and Oct. 2026. According to the recall, the affected space heaters can overheat and catch fire. DREO said they received 17 reports of ignition, three resulting in property damage and one burning a person’s hand. Anyone with a recalled unit should stop using the space heater immediately and contact DREO for a free space heater to replace the faulty one. items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. Stewart’s diagnoses had not been previously disclosed. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the “X-Men” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation” series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of “A Christmas Carol” and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” and Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen. items.t: Aging Untold: How to spot the early signs of Parkinson’s and when to talk to a doctor
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we examine the subtle, easily overlooked early warning signs of Parkinson’s disease and discuss when to talk with a physician. Plus, we explore what to consider when starting antidepressants, emphasizing the importance of setting realistic expectations and building a comprehensive support plan. Then, we share how a grieving Michigan family turned heartbreak into hope by helping pair veterans and first responders with lifesaving service dogs. Parkinson’s doesn’t always start with a tremor — here’s what to watch for Parkinson’s disease can start long before a tremor and the subtle changes are easy to miss. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the loss of smell, constipation or changes in handwriting can be early signs. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. items.t: Sisters In Survival: How a mammographer’s diagnosis led to answers for her family
items.x: GERMANTOWN, Tenn. (WMC) - As Breast Cancer Awareness Month comes to a close, one Mid-South family is sharing what can happen when one woman decides to get answers. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. items.t: Louisiana paid almost $1.2 million toward a Florida judges conference in recent years
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - For years, Louisiana judges have traveled to Florida for an annual continuing education conference. The Louisiana public has helped pick up the tab. A Fox 8 investigation studied court travel records for the annual Louisiana Judicial College (LJC) / Louisiana State Bar Association (LSBA) Summer School conference at Sandestin Golf and Beach Resort near Destin, Florida. Fox 8 attempted to compile travel cost and reimbursement records for all of Louisiana courts at the district, appellate and state supreme court levels for the years 2022 through 2025. Fox 8 did not obtain all the records for all the courts. However, the records obtained reflect responses from more than 40 courts across the state. items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections are set to be historic. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. items.t: 79-year-old man killed after collision with fire truck
items.x: WICHITA, Kan. ( KWCH /Gray News) - A 79-year-old man was killed in a crash involving a fire truck. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. The crash caused the vehicles to hit another vehicle, a black Dodge Ram. The 79-year-old man died at the hospital. He was identified by police as James Mattson of Wichita. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

( Aging Untold ) — Members of the military and first responders run toward crisis and the repeated trauma can take a serious toll on mental health. A growing number of veterans and first responders are dying by suicide, struggling with the invisible wounds of service. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. items.t: 2026 midterms set new record for political ad spending
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. items.t: 71-year-old grandmother missing after going on walk more than 3 weeks ago, police say
items.x: (Gray News) - A 71-year-old New Jersey woman went for a walk more than three weeks ago and hasn’t been seen since. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. Franklin Township police and the family are urging residents to check doorbell and security cameras for possible sightings. Anyone with information is asked to call the Franklin Township Police Department at 732-873-2300.

items.t: Two historical sculptures find a new home after sitting in storage for over a century
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - A few pieces of Savannah’s educational and architectural history found a new home at Savannah Technical College. The Savannah-Chatham County Public School System said they found two small-scale sculptures created by Savannah sculptor John Walz sitting in the attic of the Savannah-Chatham County Public School System’s Central Office Building at 208 Bull Street. Officials said the sculptures had been stored there since 1901. The sculptures are maquettes, or models, according to officials. They said Walz used them in developing the much larger figures that still overlook Oglethorpe Street from the building’s portico. They were moved from the building because of a major restoration. items.t: 79-year-old man killed after collision with fire truck
items.x: WICHITA, Kan. ( KWCH /Gray News) - A 79-year-old man was killed in a crash involving a fire truck. Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. The crash caused the vehicles to hit another vehicle, a black Dodge Ram. The 79-year-old man died at the hospital. He was identified by police as James Mattson of Wichita. The driver of the Dodge Ram was not hurt, nor were the four firefighters inside the fire truck. The WPD Critical Accident Team will investigate the crash.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: Baby dies after 15-year-old girl gives birth at elementary school, reports say
items.x: CHICAGO — Authorities are reportedly investigating the death of a baby after a teen girl gave birth at an elementary school in the Chicago area on Wednesday. Chicago police shared that a 15-year-old girl gave birth at Aldridge Elementary School on East 131st Street, but the baby was pronounced dead at the scene. WLS reports that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office listed the location of the death as 630 E. 131st St. in Chicago, which is the address for Aldridge Elementary School. The teen girl was reportedly in good condition when taken to an area hospital for treatment. Officials from the elementary school did not immediately comment on the situation, WGN reported.

items.t: 16-year-old killed in tractor crash with semi-truck, officials say
items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. Crash reports showed this was the second farm equipment crash that happened in Audubon County on Sunday. The other crash left a pickup truck driver with serious injuries after it crashed head-on with a combine.

items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. Stewart’s diagnoses had not been previously disclosed. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the “X-Men” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation” series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of “A Christmas Carol” and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” and Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen. items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — Georgia voters officially shattered the state’s all-time midterm record for early in-person voting on Thursday, surpassing the previous benchmark set in 2022. State election data shows that by Thursday afternoon, in-person turnout crossed the previous record of nearly 2.3 million ballots. The historic milestone comes the day before advance in-person voting concludes statewide. As of 1:35 p.m. Thursday, 2,294,275 Georgians had voted early, according to the secretary of state’s office. In 2022, a total of 2,289,951 people voted early in-person. With in-person and mail-in absentee ballots combined, Georgia is also poised to eclipse its record for overall midterm early turnout—a total of 2.5 million votes recorded four years ago. items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we examine the subtle, easily overlooked early warning signs of Parkinson’s disease and discuss when to talk with a physician. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

Verdict Around 6:30 p.m. Wednesday, the jury found Humphreys guilty on all five charges against him after an hour of deliberations. Humphreys, a convicted felon, faced malice murder and felony murder charges, along with multiple gun charges. The trial lasted three days, with multiple witnesses and different evidence shown to the jury. items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. More women are on state and federal ballots this cycle, with a record number running for the House of Representatives, according to Kelly Dittmar of the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. items.t: 79-year-old man killed after collision with fire truck

Police said Wichita Fire Department Engine 20 was driving with emergency lights and sirens activated when a black Honda CRV driven by the 79-year-old man entered an intersection the fire truck was crossing. The crash caused the vehicles to hit another vehicle, a black Dodge Ram. The 79-year-old man died at the hospital. He was identified by police as James Mattson of Wichita. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

WLS reports that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office listed the location of the death as 630 E. 131st St. in Chicago, which is the address for Aldridge Elementary School. items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: Glenville football removed from 2026 playoffs amid investigation
items.x: CLEVELAND, Ohio (WOIO) - Glenville High School’s football team has been removed from the 2026 football playoffs amid an investigation, the Ohio High School Athletic Association announced Thursday. The investigation came about after Ginn Academy students were inaccurately assigned to Glenville Academy for student participation opportunities, OHSAA said. Ginn Academy is a non-member magnet school that does not offer sports; however, students may participate in athletics at the Cleveland Metropolitan school that is closest to their home. Glenville’s first-round opponent, University School, will now advance to the second round on Nov. 6, OHSAA said. The announcement comes about shortly after two Glenville football players were charged with theft after allegedly stealing merchandise from a Dick’s Sporting Goods in Central Ohio. items.t: 16-year-old killed in tractor crash with semi-truck, officials say
items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. Crash reports showed this was the second farm equipment crash that happened in Audubon County on Sunday. The other crash left a pickup truck driver with serious injuries after it crashed head-on with a combine.

items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. items.t: Airbnb activates ‘anti-party technology’ in cities across the U.S.
items.x: CLEVELAND, Ohio (WOIO) - Airbnb has activated its “anti-party technology” in cities across the U.S., including Cleveland, for Halloween weekend. The technology identifies certain higher-risk bookings to help enforce the company’s year-round ban on disruptive parties. An Airbnb official said the technology helped deter about 145 people in Cleveland from booking an entire home during Halloween weekend in 2025. It is the fifth year the company has used the technology. Airbnb already bans disruptive parties worldwide, but the company cracks down more during certain times of year, including Halloween. items.t: Oberlin murder suspect bound over after prosecutor details alleged video admission
items.x: LORAIN COUNTY, Ohio (WOIO) - The person accused of killing an Oberlin College professor and his wife appeared in court Thursday, where a judge set bond at $3 million and bound the case over to Lorain County Common Pleas Court. Asia Nguyen-Duy, 31, of Ashland, Oregon, faces six counts of murder, four counts of felonious assault and one count of tampering with evidence. Nguyen-Duy previously went by Daniel Jones. Court records show they legally changed their name in 2025. During Thursday’s hearing, Nguyen-Duy said they are gender-neutral and prefer to be called Asia Nguyen-Duy. The victims were identified as 64-year-old Pipo Nguyen-Duy and 56-year-old Thi Tran Phong. Oberlin College and Conservatory identified Pipo Nguyen-Duy as a beloved professor of studio art and photography who taught at the college for many years. items.t: Space heaters under recall after units reportedly catch fire
items.x: (Gray News) - Almost 340,000 space heaters are under recall throughout the United States due to the risk of fire and burns. DREO space heaters model DR-HSH015 were placed under recall on Oct. 29, the Consumer Product Safety Commission reported. About 338,800 units were affected, with an additional 36,300 sold in Canada. They were sold directly through DREO and other sites like Best Buy and Home Depot between Sept. 2025 and Oct. 2026. According to the recall, the affected space heaters can overheat and catch fire. DREO said they received 17 reports of ignition, three resulting in property damage and one burning a person’s hand. Anyone with a recalled unit should stop using the space heater immediately and contact DREO for a free space heater to replace the faulty one. items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. Stewart’s diagnoses had not been previously disclosed. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the “X-Men” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation” series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of “A Christmas Carol” and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” and Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen. items.x: CLEVELAND, Ohio (WOIO) - There are just days before the Nov. 3rd election and records are being shattered for the amount of Ohioans voting early in-person at their county board of elections. In 2018, 177,046 total had voted early, in person the week before the election according to the Ohio Secretary of State, Frank LaRose. In 2022, that number was 265,062 votes. As of Wednesday morning, 770,601 people have already voted in the 2026 mid-term elections in Ohio. According to Case Western Reserve University professor Jonathan Entin there are a couple of reasons for the explosion of votes. For one, the ease and comfortability of people going to their board of elections and getting their votes recorded. Another possibility, people may fear putting their ballots in the mail. items.t: Former Northeast Ohio high school band director indicted by grand jury
items.x: STARK COUNTY, Ohio (WOIO) — The former band director at Northwest High School in Canal Fulton was indicted by a Stark County Grand Jury. Stephen Imler was indicted on three charges of sexual battery and one charge of grooming. He will be arraigned on Oct. 30. Imler, who was also a music teacher at the high school, was placed on administrative leave on Aug. 18 when the allegations were first announced. On Sept. 2n, Imler officially resigned from both positions. He was arrested by members of the U.S. Marshals Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force on Oct. 23. According to U.S. Marshal Pete Elliott, Imler was taken into custody without incident at a home in the 4600 block of Hametown Rd. in Norton.

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. Stewart’s diagnoses had not been previously disclosed. items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: Understanding ‘fall fatigue’ and how to push through
items.x: LAKE CHARLES, La. (KPLC) - Fall fatigue: It’s when you feel less focused, moody, and downright tired. Experts say it’s normal this time of year, especially with the time change this weekend. But there are things you can do to push through. The days are shorter, the mornings darker. And if you’re in a slump, it may be the season. Sleep medicine doctor Chafen Hart with National Jewish Health says, “The hardest times are these dark weeks right before we change back to Standard Time because it’s still so dark in the morning hours.” Fall fatigue can happen when your body can’t process the sudden change to more darkness during the day. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans

The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. items.t: 2026 midterms set new record for political ad spending
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. items.t: World Stroke Day: Former firefighter turns stroke survival into lifelong mission of hope
items.x: WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - For more than three decades, William “Bill” Blenk was the person running toward danger, saving lives as a firefighter and training the next generation as an EMT instructor. But 21 years ago, life flipped in an instant when he became the one who needed saving. He was 64 when a stroke took away his ability to do the simplest daily tasks. “I could not talk. I could not write. I could not eat. I had to learn how to eat,” he said. His wife, Pat, said she still remembers the terrifying moment it started. “He said, ‘Pat, Pat, something’s gravely wrong.’ I said, ‘What’s wrong?’ And then he had the weakness starting. And when we got to the hospital, he couldn’t talk,” she said. Faced with a sudden silence, Pat found a way to bridge the gap. items.t: Fire officials say commercial building fire near Shallotte not related to other fires
items.x: SHALLOTTE, N.C. (WECT) - A fire at Ike’s Pit off Old Georgetown Road took more than four hours to bring under control Wednesday evening. [PREVIOUS STORY: Fire off Old Georgetown Road in Brunswick County under control] The Shallotte Point Volunteer Fire Department responded around 6:30 p.m. Fire Department Chief Buddy Causey said welding equipment stored inside the building caused several explosions as the fire burned. Blasts could be heard in the area and smoke filled the sky. “There were a few explosions,” Causey said. “[The owner] had welding equipment and stuff inside the building, so some of the bottles were exploding inside the building during the fire.” Officials said the fire was unrelated to previous fires in the area or to the large wildfires earlier this year. Workers at Ike’s Pit declined an on-camera interview. No injuries were reported.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. items.t: ‘Star Trek’ actor Patrick Stewart dead at 86
items.x: (AP) - Patrick Stewart , the classically trained actor who added Shakespearean gravitas to the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. items.x: HUEYTOWN, Ala. ( WBRC ) - Two people were airlifted two a hospital after a crash in Hueytown Thursday, police said. According to Hueytown Police, a garbage truck and car were involved in a wreck on John’s Road near a water treatment facility. Police said four people were in the car and all suffered injuries. Officials said two of them were airlifted to a hospital with life-threatening injuries and the other two were taken to a hospital by ambulance. Women make up 50% of the population and are the most consistent voting bloc in American elections, even though women have only been able to legally cast a ballot for just over a century. items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The 2026 midterm elections have become the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history when it comes to political advertising, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election. With Election Day less than a week away, an estimated $11.21 billion has been spent or reserved for political advertisements, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. That’s slightly more than the $11.2 billion spent during the entire 2024 election cycle and roughly $2.3 billion more than the 2022 midterms. “It’s not just that a lot of money is being spent, it’s that it’s very expensive to advertise this late in the campaign,” said Todd Belt, a political management professor at George Washington University. items.x: (Gray News) - A 71-year-old New Jersey woman went for a walk more than three weeks ago and hasn’t been seen since. Belinda Prentice was last seen about 6 p.m. Oct. 5 near Bamburgh Court off New Brunswick Road and Willow Avenue in Franklin Township, a press release said. Her granddaughter, Sienna Benjamin, said Prentice had shown signs of cognitive decline in recent years, and the family was working to determine whether she had dementia and to obtain guardianship, People reported. Franklin Township police and the family are urging residents to check doorbell and security cameras for possible sightings. Anyone with information is asked to call the Franklin Township Police Department at 732-873-2300.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before next weekend’s time change.

items.t: Baby dies after 15-year-old girl gives birth at elementary school, reports say
items.x: CHICAGO — Authorities are reportedly investigating the death of a baby after a teen girl gave birth at an elementary school in the Chicago area on Wednesday. Chicago police shared that a 15-year-old girl gave birth at Aldridge Elementary School on East 131st Street, but the baby was pronounced dead at the scene. WLS reports that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office listed the location of the death as 630 E. 131st St. in Chicago, which is the address for Aldridge Elementary School. items.t: 16-year-old killed in tractor crash with semi-truck, officials say
items.x: AUDUBON, Iowa ( KCRG /Gray News) - A teen is dead after being thrown from a tractor in a crash with a semi-truck. Iowa State Patrol said it happened Sunday night on Highway 71, just south of Audubon. A crash report said a semi-truck hit the back of the trailer that the tractor was pulling. Tatum Christensen, 16, was ejected from the tractor. He died at the scene. The report said the semi-truck driver was flown to the hospital with serious injuries. Crash reports showed this was the second farm equipment crash that happened in Audubon County on Sunday. The other crash left a pickup truck driver with serious injuries after it crashed head-on with a combine.

items.t: Legendary college football coach June Jones dies at 73
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) - Former University of Hawaii head football coach June Jones has died at the age of 73, according to multiple sources Thursday. June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999 through 2007. He went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014. Jones led Hawaii to six bowl games and coached three seasons with 10 or more wins, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and a trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and a share of the Western Athletic Conference title and earned him National Coach of the Year honors. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said.
